question: Distinguish between an ordinary resolution and a special resolution under the Companies Act, 2013.
sources: Companies Act, 2013 - section 114 ordinary and special resolutions

points.label: Ordinary resolution
points.description: Passed when the notice required under the Act has been duly given and the votes cast in favour (on a show of hands, electronically or on a poll, including the chairman's casting vote, if any) are more than the votes cast against by members entitled to vote.

points.label: Special resolution: stated in the notice
points.description: The intention to propose the resolution as a special resolution must be clearly stated in the notice of the meeting or other intimation to members.

points.label: Special resolution: notice duly given
points.description: The notice required under the Act must have been duly given.

points.label: Special resolution: three-fourths majority
points.description: The votes cast in favour by members entitled to vote, in person, by proxy or by postal ballot, must be at least three times the votes cast against.
